subject: Learning Methods
title: Notification Hijacking
description: A fast breakdown of Notification Hijacking for builders.

hook.text: The average person checks their phone 96 times a day. Each check hijacks attention for an average of 23 minutes.

buildup.text: Notifications exploit bottom-up attention. The buzz, the badge, the preview all trigger a dopamine-driven urge to check.

discovery.text: Even resisting a notification costs mental energy. The knowledge that a message is waiting drains working memory.

twist.text: Turning off sound is not enough. Visible badges and lock-screen previews create the same pull. Eliminate all cues.

climax.text: During study sessions, put your phone in another room. Out of sight genuinely means out of mind for your brain.

punchline.text: A phone in the room lowers your IQ. Move it away.

quiz.question: Why is turning off notification sounds not sufficient?
options: Sound is not a real distraction
Visible badges and previews create the same attentional pull
The phone still vibrates even on silent mode
